protocol.question: Does carrying inherited split lower bounds in GPU nearest-candidate traversal reduce full production C2C operation time?
protocol.shaderChange: Near child retains the inherited lower bound; far child retains max(parent lower bound, local split distance squared). This is a rounded f32 hint only. Exact f64 verification remains authoritative.
protocol.orderScheme: Alternate local/inherited and inherited/local; six timed pairs per position per report; retain all tails
protocol.timed: Ordinary production loaded-cloud C2C RPC: fresh query snapshot, GPU dispatch/readback, four streaming exact CPU worker lanes, ordered statistics, f32 export, normal asynchronous release submission and result transfer
protocol.excluded: Input parse/index, pool/device/reference/pipeline initialization, diagnostics and CPU oracle checks
protocol.defaultChangeGate: Adopt inherited bounds in ordinary GPU C2C only if every one of four reports has at least 1% median paired reduction and at least 7/12 faster pairs. Otherwise retain local split bounds.
protocol.correctness: Every displayed f32 distance bit and ordered summary field must equal the indexed-cloud CPU oracle. Each control must have stable certificate counts across its trials; candidate slots and certificate counts may differ between shader controls. No timed fallback or reference rebuild. Untimed browser checks cover full f64 verification against brute force and direct shader split/partial/concurrent/variant behavior.
protocol.wasmReuse: Rust and Cargo files remain unchanged. Reuse only if all prior normalized Rust input hashes and all four WASM/glue/type artifact hashes match; rebuild the production frontend and capture its current sources/artifacts before timing. CI rebuilds WASM normally.
protocol.safety: No adapter identity, unchanged real measured source maps, no generated timing geometry, no heavy work during timing, no nightly/toolchain downloads.

limitations: The comparison changes rounded GPU candidate traversal only. All final distances remain under the existing authoritative f64 verifier.

Candidate slots and certificate counts may differ between shader variants; each variant must have stable counts across trials. In these four reports both variants had identical certificate counts, also matching the preceding production packet.

Full-operation timing includes a fresh query snapshot, physical GPU, four streaming exact CPU lanes, ordered statistics, f32 export and ordinary asynchronous release submission; excludes input parse/index and pool/device/reference/pipeline initialization.
The same verified Rust/WASM binary is reused. Current JS/WGSL and all build sources are captured after a frontend rebuild. CI additionally exercises this reuse following a full WASM build.

The full f64 query-coordinate diagnostic uses raw parsed order. The production RPC checks all displayed f32 bits and ordered f64 summary fields against its indexed-cloud CPU oracle. Untimed browser fixtures additionally compare full f64 distances to brute force.
All tails are retained. CPU/GPU clocks, host activity, GC and power are uncontrolled. Host GPU wait is not isolated shader execution time.
Timing inputs are byte-identical unchanged measured point subsets, not independent surveys or SLAM ground truth. Synthetic edge cases are used only for untimed correctness tests.

The application indexes loaded clouds. Certificate counts and displayed-order hashes must not be pooled with standalone shared-verifier studies using different preparation. No adapter identity is collected.
